definitions.explanation: Being excessively serious or earnest to the point of inflexibility. Often implies someone who lacks humor, is rigid in their thinking, or takes everything too literally.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{生真面目|きまじめ}で{冗談|じょうだん}が{通|つう}じない。
examples.english: He's so serious that jokes go right over his head.

examples.japanese: {生真面目|きまじめ}に{考|かんが}えすぎないで。
examples.english: Don't think about it too seriously.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{生真面目|きまじめ}な{性格|せいかく}だから、{融通|ゆうずう}が{利|き}かない。
examples.english: That person is so strait-laced that they can't be flexible.

notes:
FORMATION:
{生|き} (prefix intensifying meaning) + {真面目|まじめ} (serious, earnest)

The {生|き} prefix intensifies {真面目|まじめ} to mean 'excessively' or 'overly' serious.

USAGE:
・{生真面目|きまじめ}な{人|ひと}/{性格|せいかく} (an overly serious person/personality)
・{生真面目|きまじめ}に{受|う}け{止|と}める (to take something too seriously)

NUANCE:
While {真面目|まじめ} (serious, earnest) is generally positive, {生真面目|きまじめ} carries a slightly negative nuance of being too rigid, humorless, or inflexible. It suggests someone who could benefit from loosening up.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{真面目|まじめ} - Serious, earnest (neutral to positive)
・{堅|かた}い - Stiff, formal, uptight
・{杓子定規|しゃくしじょうぎ} - Inflexible, going by the book
